 Duckett and Dawson earn England consolation win over Sri Lanka in ODI tri-series

 LAHORE, Pakistan (AP) — Ben Duckett’s second straight century and Liam Dawson’s career-best 4-49 earned England a 55-run consolation win over Sri Lanka in a cricket tri-series Thursday.
 Duckett’s career-best 167 off 132 balls propelled England to 386-5 — the highest-ever ODI score at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore — after Kusal Mendis won his seventh successive toss on the tour and elected to field.

 Pavan Rathnayake followed his century in Sri Lanka’s astonishing run-chase against England at Rawalpindi last week with 118 off 77 balls before falling to Dawson in the 45th over as Sri Lanka got bowled out for 331.
 It was England’s first ODI win in Pakistan since 2005 after it lost its first three games in this tri-series and was already out of contention for Saturday’s final.
 Last week, England captain Harry Brook’s fastest-ever ODI double-century wasn’t enough to stop Sri Lanka from successfully chasing down the second highest-ever total of 430 runs in the 50-over format.
 Shadab Khan trumped Duckett's hundred and smashed an extraordinary 113 off 96 balls in Pakistan’s epic one-wicket win at Lahore on Sunday after England had reduced the home team to 154-9 in a chase of 242.
 England crashed to 87-run defeat in its opening match against Pakistan after cruising to 120-1 in a chase 303-run target at Rawalpindi.
 Rathnayake's third ODI century against England this year kept Sri Lanka in the hunt for another big chase in the tournament after Mendis opted to field for the fourth consecutive time.
 Mendis made 89 off 71 balls and rebuilt the chase with 84-run second-wicket stand with Avishka Fernando, who scored 48, after Kamindu Mendis was clean bowled by Sonny Baker in the fourth over for 4.
 Dawson broke the stand in the 17th over when Fernando was caught by Will Jacks on the edge of extra cover boundary but Mendis and Rathnayake kept on accelerating with another 80-run partnership.
 Brook turned to Joe Root in the 27th over and the off-spinner struck when Mendis got a faint edge to wicketkeeper while trying to sweep. Rathnayake then took charge and together with Janith Liyanage, who struck three sixes in his cameo of 27, and Sahan Arachchige (30) added half-century stands as bowlers found it difficult to grip the wet ball because of dew.
 But Dawson took the game away from Sri Lanka when Rathnayake, who hit 15 fours and a six, miscued a sweep against the left-arm spinner and top-edged to fine leg as England claimed the last three wickets for three runs for its first win.
 Duckett’s sixth ODI hundred and Tom Banton’s 74 off 75 balls gave England a strong platform of finishing big as they shared 163-run opening stand in 25 overs.
 Brook, batting at No. 3 for the first time in ODIs, made 44 and put on another brisk 107 off 75 balls with Duckett as they carried England to 270-2 in the 38th over.
 Duckett continued his fine form by playing some exquisite shots with 17 of his 24 boundaries coming on the leg-side of the wicket as he surpassed his previous ODI best of 165 made against Australia at the same Gaddafi Stadium during the Champions Trophy last year.
 He completed his century off 89 balls and then upped the ante with Brook. Asitha Fernando (2-63) was the pick of the bowlers and dismissed Brook when the England captain tried to scoop the pace bowler but got a leading edge and offered a return catch.
 Duckett soon followed when he scooped Sri Lanka’s most expensive bowler Eshan Malinga (1-101) to short fine leg in the 42nd over, but England still managed to score 94 runs off the final 10 overs.
 Jacks made 30 off 21 balls while Jordon Cox scored 43 off 27 balls and Sam Curran was unbeaten on 21.

 United States Signs Participation Contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh, Strengthening Momentum For Global Participation
 ATLANTA & RIYADH, Saudi Arabia--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct 31, 2026--
 The United States of America has signed its Participation Contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh, marking a significant milestone in the World Expo’s preparations and further strengthening the momentum for international participation in the global event.
 This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261031669001/en/
 The signing marks an important step in the United States’ journey towards Expo 2030 Riyadh, paving the way for the development of its pavilion, programming and visitor experience. It also reinforces the growing international commitment to Expo 2030 Riyadh, as countries move from confirming their participation to actively shaping the experiences, ideas and innovations they will bring to the Kingdom in 2030.
 The Participation Contract was signed by His Highness Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, during a bilateral meeting held on the sidelines of the 2026 G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, Georgia. The signing ceremony was attended by Her Royal Highness Princess Reema bint Bandar bin Sultan bin Abdulaziz Al-Saud, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to the United States, and Talal Al-Marri, CEO of Expo 2030 Riyadh.
 Building on its longstanding tradition of participation in World Expos, the United States will develop its presence on a dedicated plot within Expo 2030 Riyadh’s Technology precinct. Its participation will offer an opportunity to showcase American innovation, creativity and technological leadership, while contributing to the Expo’s theme, “Foresight for Tomorrow.”
 The United States joins a growing number of countries that have formalised their participation in Expo 2030 Riyadh, reflecting continued progress in international engagement. More than 185 Official Participants have confirmed participation, with preparations advancing across pavilion planning, content development and programming. Each new contract marks a further step in translating international commitments into a robust and compelling World Expo experience.
 Meanwhile, work continues to progress across the Expo site in northern Riyadh, with infrastructure development and construction of key assets advancing. Together, these milestones demonstrate the progress being made on both fronts: building the physical foundations of Expo 2030 Riyadh and bringing together the international participants who will shape its content and visitor experience.
 Held under the theme “Foresight for Tomorrow,” Expo 2030 Riyadh will take place from 1 October 2030 to 31 March 2031 , bringing together countries and international organisations from around the world and welcoming more than 42 million visits over six months. Through its five thematic areas - Technology, Planet, Humanity, Culture and Collaboration - the Expo will provide a global platform for nations to share their achievements and ambitions, explore solutions to shared challenges and inspire new possibilities for the future.
 About Expo 2030 Riyadh 
 Running from 1 October 2030 to 31 March 2031, Expo 2030 Riyadh will be among the most ambitious World Expos ever conceived with a 6 million square meter site that will bring together 197 Official Participants and is expected to welcome 42 million visits across 5 distinct districts.
 Held under the theme “Foresight for Tomorrow,” and hosted in Riyadh - a city of action and ambition - Expo 2030 Riyadh will provide a platform for participants to exchange ideas, shape solutions, and build partnerships that drive real impact, address global challenges, and unlock new opportunities. The World Expo will feature immersive cultural zones, daily activations, and AI-powered interactions, blending traditional Saudi hospitality with cutting-edge technology. Following the six-month event, the Expo site will evolve into a vibrant destination, continuing to attract visitors and contribute to Riyadh’s dynamic urban landscape.
 For more information, please visit: https://www.expo2030riyadh.sa/en/
